newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SKF next in line for shakeup - analysts.
newsitem.headline: SKF next in line for shakeup - analysts.

text.p: Swedish bearings-maker SKF was on Monday earmarked by analysts as the next company in the powerful Wallenberg empire set for restructuring following appliance-maker Electrolux's radical shakeup.
Analysts said Electrolux's announced restructure, which includes cutting 12,000 jobs and closing 25 plants worldwide, was likely to trigger more changes in the Wallenberg stable.
"The positive market reaction to the Electrolux programme has put pressure on other company leaders in the Wallenberg stable to do something," said Mats Liss, Swedbank analyst.
A 16 percent rise in SKF's share price since Electrolux unveiled its plans on June 12 was taken as a sign that the market wanted to see similar action in the bearings company.
On Monday afternoon SKF shares were trading 1.5 crowns lower at 212.5 crowns, off a recent high of 216 crowns.
"Market speculation has lifted SKF's share price since Electrolux announced its programme. There is likely to be changes in SKF," said Dresdner Kleinwort Benson analyst Peter Lawrence.
Analysts said SKF had recently shown weak profit development and an inability to live up to the market's expectations.
SKF's profit after financial items in the first quarter was 23 percent lower than expected.
One way to tackle its problems would be to cut both the number of production units and the workforce, said analysts.
"SKF has a lot of production units and many staff so it should be possible to concentrate more," said one analyst.
SKF is due to release its six-month report on Tuesday. It planned to hold an analysts' meeting at 0600 GMT.
A Reuters poll of analysts found expectations of half-year profit falling to 1.13 billion crowns compared to 1.48 billion crowns at the same time a year earlier.
The company declined to comment on the contents of the half- year report.

"There is continuously an ongoing process to see whether anything can be done to improve operations. A lot has been done already but in every company this is always an ongoing process," said SKF spokesman Lars Malmer.
But even if SKF were to present a package of change, it would probably not be as radical as the restructuring announced by Electrolux, analysts said.

"There are not really the same possibilities in SKF as in Electrolux as SKF streamlined a lot during the downturn in the economy in the early 1990s. SKF has done more than Electrolux," said one analyst.
Analysts did not think that other Wallenberg companies would announce extensive restructuring programmes like Electrolux because they were not in need of such change.

Drugs major Astra and telecoms group Ericsson are growth companies, industrial engineer Atlas Copco is profitable and well-managed and forestry company Stora is less people-intensive so would find it harder to make big cuts.
